first_impression.reaction: My assistant found it searching Bali venues. The first screen is calm, there are no prices and nothing about 'dream' anything, and the table puts exclusive use in its own column, which is the column I care about. Most of the list is sized for 30 to 100 people, though. Her summary would be 'Samabe and COMO are the only published buy-outs, AYANA and Grand Hyatt have the space for 300, Bvlgari's beach is private, nothing on security'. I read the takeaways, the table, the clifftops, Nusa Dua, the guest-count table, exclusive use, travel and the close.

journey.section: Bali wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: Honest. I would rather see a gap than a guess. But that column is almost entirely 'Not published', which tells me the real answers come from a phone call, not this page.

journey.quote: Only a few venues publish a full resort buy-out, including Samabe and the two COMO properties, so ask every venue the same questions about exclusive use in writing.
journey.reaction: Two COMO properties? I only see COMO Uma Ubud on the page. My assistant would flag that straight away, and it makes me wonder what else is loose.

journey.quote: Its [weddings collection](https://www.ayana.com/bali/weddings/) names four packages, from a villa wedding to a cliffside wedding at Tresna.
journey.reaction: Packages. That is the first thing said about the venue. I am not choosing from a set menu.

journey.quote: Ceremony and reception figures are set out separately for every space, from Rock Bar (reception 20) to Champa Garden (ceremony 800, reception 3,000).
journey.reaction: This is a property that can physically take us. Good to know early.

journey.quote: The beach and beachside restaurant below the cliff are reserved for in-house guests and reached only by the resort's inclined elevator.
journey.reaction: One way in, guests only. That is the kind of detail my security people want. Then capacity and exclusive use are both 'not published', so I learn nothing about whether it fits us.

journey.quote: An exclusive buy-out reserves the entire resort for your event, including two nights of accommodation for 260 guests, and every member of staff is dedicated to the event.
journey.reaction: The whole resort closed, every member of staff ours, and it sleeps 260. This is the only line on the page written for a wedding like mine. My assistant would put it at the top.

journey.quote: The pillar-less Grand Ballroom (1,202 square metres) seats 736 for a banquet and the Karangasem ballroom 320; the outdoor wedding space is listed for 1,500 guests.
journey.reaction: Space, yes. But a large Nusa Dua chain hotel full of other guests is the opposite of discreet unless it can be closed, and that is 'not published'.

journey.quote: For the night before, the Mezzanine of Kayuputi, the upper level of the fine-dining restaurant, takes up to 20 for a rehearsal dinner.
journey.reaction: Twenty people for the night before. Our immediate family alone is more than that. Skipped.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: For every other venue, ask whether the wedding spaces, or the whole property, can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: The right question. I would expect whoever I hire to already have that answer for each of these, not hand it back to me.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
journey.reaction: This is written for a couple sending a group chat to their friends. Our guests' travel is handled by people whose job that is.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Does the venue arrange guest transport, and for how many guests?
journey.reaction: Fine as far as it goes, but no mention of private transfers, VIP arrivals at the airport or security at all. With 300 guests, some of them known, that is the first thing my family office would ask.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?
journey.quote: Persons of any nationality may generally marry in Indonesia if they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government, listed as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian, and both parties must hold the same religion.
journey.reaction: Stated plainly, without assumptions about who I am. Useful for the family conversation about where the legal ceremony happens.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One contact suits me; fewer people, fewer leaks. But 'for Australian couples' tells me straight away I am not who this is written for, and nothing shows they have done a wedding at our size.

unanswered_questions: Have you delivered a Bali wedding, or any wedding, for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
Who would be on the ground in Bali for us, and do you have existing relationships with Samabe, AYANA or Bvlgari? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private airport arrivals, transfers and coordination between our security team and the venue's? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, can you quote in a currency other than AUD, and do you work through a family office? (deferred business detail)
What access comes with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Which of these venues besides Samabe and COMO Uma Ubud can actually be closed to the public, and for how many nights?
Can Bvlgari or AYANA be taken exclusively for a guest list of 300, and do they sleep that many?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, drones, outside photographers, staff phones and social media?
Which is the second COMO property the takeaways mention?

turn_offs_found.quote: Its [weddings collection](https://www.ayana.com/bali/weddings/) names four packages, from a villa wedding to a cliffside wedding at Tresna.
turn_offs_found.why: Package language. Leading a venue description with its set packages makes me feel like a standard client choosing from a brochure.

turn_offs_found.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining traveller basics. It lowers the register for a family whose guests' travel is handled for them.

turn_offs_found.quote: There have been cases of methanol poisoning in Bali, so serve and order only branded alcohol.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Telling a host to serve branded alcohol reads as a backpacker warning, not advice for a private event with its own caterer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
turn_offs_found.why: Frames the service around a standard Australian couple. I live in Dubai, and it signals I am outside the audience.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the Samabe buy-out line, the Bvlgari private beach line, the AYANA and Grand Hyatt capacities and the exclusive-use question in the planning file, and forward the volcano and flight-disruption lines to whoever handles guest travel. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Bali venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=bali-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a blog link. The page is calm and honest about what venues don't publish, which I respect, but it says nothing about security, private transfers or work at our scale, and it is addressed to Australian couples. I'd want a private introduction first.

top_3_changes: Fix the key takeaway that says 'the two COMO properties' when only COMO Uma Ubud appears; a factual slip on the first screen costs trust with a reader who checks.

Add a privacy and security line to the exclusive-use and transport sections, phrased as questions to ask each venue (private airport arrivals, closing the property to other guests, working with the couple's own security, drones and outside photographers), without claiming anything about Wedded Wonderland's own delivery.
Trim traveller basics for readers who delegate: shorten the passport-damage and methanol lines to one pointer to Smartraveller, and lead AYANA's entry with its spaces rather than its packages.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

No invented brand facts; scale proof, ground team, transfers, security, fees, currency and Privileges listed in unanswered_questions as deferred

open_questions.question: The key takeaway names 'the two COMO properties' but the draft features only COMO Uma Ubud. Please route to the editor or fact-checker: either a second COMO venue was cut or the takeaway is wrong.
The draft never mentions security, VIP arrivals or press and drone privacy. Layla asks for these as questions to put to venues, not as brand claims. Weigh against the 0.20 persona weight.
